problem_statement: With multiple mbuf pools, allocation must continue past an empty size-suitable pool when a larger pool has free buffers. A zero requested size must select the largest pool that has available buffers.
extra_warnings:
Use the supplied tests as the acceptance oracle. Do not add, remove, or modify tests or test helpers.
Do not modify get_msys_pool_list or its SELFTEST wrapper; it is protected upstream test support.

verification.reason: The statement omits a required public accessor and some observable allocation behaviours that the hidden tests depend on, but these can be added as public interface/behaviour requirements without dictating the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden self-test code calls get_msys_pool_list() and expects it to return the current msys mbuf pool list, but the problem statement does not mention this function, its return type, or that it must expose the actual list used by msys.

The hidden allocation cases include requests larger than all registered pool data lengths and expect allocation from the largest pool that has a free buffer; the statement only mentions empty size-suitable pools and zero-size requests, not this oversized-request behaviour.
The hidden cases check that a nonzero request is served by the smallest suitable non-empty pool before continuing to larger pools, but the statement does not state this selection rule explicitly.

leak_check.leak_detail: The statement is mostly behavioral and interface-level, but it hints at implementation by specifying the selection procedure in detail and by requiring the accessor to be provided under SELFTEST. These are minor hints, not a direct leak of code or the internal variable.
leak_check.suggested_statement:
With multiple mbuf pools, allocation must continue past an empty size-suitable pool when a larger pool has free buffers. A zero requested size must select the largest pool that has available buffers.

For a nonzero requested data size, allocation must use the smallest pool that can accommodate the requested size and has a free buffer. If that pool has no free buffer, allocation must continue to the next larger pool with a free buffer. If no pool can accommodate the requested size, allocation must use the largest free pool; if no pool has a free buffer, allocation must fail.

The change must also expose the current msys mbuf pool list via get_msys_pool_list(), returning a pointer to that list (struct os_mbuf_list *), referring to the list updated by os_msys_register.
